Identity.title: Identity
Identity.description: How a principal authenticates: a provider's stable subject bound to a Member (an operator) or a Person (an end user), with the asserted email and the kinds of factor used. Credential material lives in the auth store, never here.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

provider.description: builtin, or the issuer URL of an external provider

email.description: the address this login asserts; never a key

factors.description: the kinds of credential used; device and enrolment details live in the auth store

last_seen_at.description: touched at most once an hour; drives the monthly active user count

x-model.name: identity
x-model.agent_context:
Identity is written by the auth component when someone signs in; you never create or edit one. A Person with an
Identity is an end user. Dedupe by (provider, subject); an email is never an Identity key, only a Person one.
The one mistake: looking for passwords or tokens here; credentials are never stored on records.

Import run.title: Import run
Import run.description: One execution of an importer: which importer, in which mode, with what outcome and per-model counts. Every record it wrote carries its id in source.import_run.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

x-model.name: import_run
x-model.agent_context:
An ImportRun is created by the import_run tool or POST /v1/imports, never by hand; read it for the counts and the errors, and
always run with dry_run first. Find what a run wrote by querying source.import_run. The one mistake: retrying a
partial run without reading its errors; the rows that succeeded are already upserted and simply update again.

Member.title: Member
Member.description: An operator of the workspace: a person on the team, an agent or a service, with roles. Authorization, audit and the owner and assignee fields point at Members.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

roles.description: owner, admin, member, or a custom role name that policies grant

invitation.description: set while status is invited; the magic link sent to this email activates the Member

x-model.name: member
x-model.agent_context:
Member is who operates the workspace, including you: an agent runs as the Member its API key was created for.
End users of the product are never Members; they are Persons with an Identity, and a guest is a Person with a
Share, not a role. Dedupe by person, or by the invitation email while invited. The one mistake: creating a
Member to represent a customer or a contact; create a Person instead.

Policy.title: Policy
Policy.description: A rule: which principals may do which actions on which model, narrowed by a filter in the query grammar. Packs ship defaults, admins edit them, Shares compile into them.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

value.description: the role name for role, the share id for share

principal.description: the class of caller the policy applies to

applies_to.description: a model name, or * for every model

where.description: a where object of the query grammar; variables @principal.person, @principal.member, @principal.identity, @principal.affiliated_organizations, @share.id, @now

fields.description: field allow-list for read or update

x-model.name: policy
x-model.agent_context:
Policies are ANDed into every read and write by end users, guests and the public; members are governed by roles
and never consult them. Only admins write Policies. Dedupe by name. The one mistake: a `where` written against
fields the model in applies_to does not have; run it as a query first.

Share.title: Share
Share.description: A grant of read, and optionally comment, access to records, by ids or by filter, to someone outside the workspace: a link, an email, another workspace or the public. Compiles into Policies for a synthetic principal.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

x-model.name: share
x-model.agent_context:
Share is how records leave the workspace without being copied. Content is published by the Content pack's public
policy (a Collection with public: true), the same shape a public Share compiles to. Scope by filter when the set
changes over time, by ids when it is fixed. Comment is granted to email grantees only: a Note has an author. A link token is returned once at creation and lives in the credential store, never on the record.
The one mistake: deleting a Share to revoke it; set status to revoked, which keeps the audit trail.

Tag.title: Tag
Tag.description: A label that works the same on every record: a namespaced slug with a display name, a colour and a description. The envelope's tags[] holds slugs that resolve to Tag records.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

name.description: the display form; may carry case and spaces

namespace.description: none = workspace-local; sys, a pack name and a source name are reserved

applies_to.description: model names this tag is meant for; absent means any

x-model.name: tag
x-model.agent_context:
Tags classify; they never carry meaning the standard depends on (that is a field or a Status). Write slugs in
tags[] on any record and missing workspace tags are created for you; create a Tag record only to set a colour or
a description. A slug is [namespace:]segment(/segment)*, each segment [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}, at most 255
characters, compared case-insensitively; name is the display form. Dedupe by (namespace, slug). The one mistake:
writing into a reserved namespace (sys, a pack name, a source name); those belong to the server, packs and importers.

Workspace.title: Workspace
Workspace.description: The tenant: one company or one person, holding exactly one of these records, its first. Holds the installed packs and the members, identities, policies, shares, tags and records.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

slug.description: URL-safe, unique per server or platform

allowed_email_domains.description: when set, only these domains may sign up as end users

allowed_redirect_uris.description: redirect URIs the magic-link and OAuth flows may return to; localhost is always allowed

signup.description: whether an unknown email may create an end user

member_role_claim_values.description: role name to claim value, for member issuers

auto_join.description: for member issuers: add anyone the issuer vouches for as a Member; off means invited or bound people only

issuers.description: external OIDC issuers this workspace trusts

x-model.name: workspace
x-model.agent_context:
Workspace is the tenant. You never create one; provisioning does, and a workspace holds exactly one of these
records. Read it for the installed packs and the sign-in settings. Dedupe by slug. The one mistake: updating auth
without reading it first; the object is replaced whole on update.

Event.title: Event
Event.description: A scheduled block of time: a meeting, a call, an appointment, a reminder. One record per series; a logged call or meeting is an Event too.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

period.description: start inclusive; end exclusive, omitted for a zero-duration event

timezone.description: IANA zone of start and end

x-model.name: event
x-model.agent_context:
Event is anything with a time slot, past or future; the timeline of a Deal or a Ticket is a query over the Events,
Messages, Notes and Tasks about it. Give a recurring Event its IANA timezone so local times survive daylight
saving; one Recurrence rule per series, exceptions are ext.calendar.*. Dedupe by the iCalendar uid identifier
(system ical:uid). The one mistake: an attendee as free text when a Person or Member exists; set attendees[].ref.

File.title: File
File.description: Stored or referenced binary content with a name and a type. The bytes live in object storage or on disk; the record holds the name, type, size and location.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

mime_type.description: detected by the server; importers fall back to the extension or application/octet-stream

size.description: bytes; absent for native cloud documents

provider.description: local, s3, or a source system

x-model.name: file
x-model.agent_context:
Create a File through the upload flow (upload-url, then complete), not by hand, so the storage key and the sha256
identifier are right. Dedupe by identifier: the server adds {system: sha256} for stored bytes; sources may add
md5, sha1, crc32, quickxor or dropbox:content-hash, and <source>:file for their own ids. The one mistake: a URL to
an external file stored as a File; a File is bytes the workspace holds or a source system stores.

Message.title: Message
Message.description: One message on a channel: an email, a chat message, an SMS, a call record, with sender, recipients, body and the records it is about. A Ticket's conversation is its Messages.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

body.description: plain text or Markdown; may be empty when the message is only attachments

thread_key.description: opaque grouping key: a mail thread id, a chat channel and thread, a ticket id

x-model.name: message
x-model.agent_context:
Message is a communication that happened or will be sent; internal commentary is a Note. Link it to the Ticket or
Deal through about and to its thread through thread_key. Dedupe by identifier: email:message-id (the Message-ID
without angle brackets) for mail, slack:ts for chat, <source>:message otherwise. The one mistake: setting
delivery on an inbound Message; delivery describes outbound sending.

Note.title: Note
Note.description: Free text about one or more records: an internal note, a comment, a meeting summary. A Note about exactly one record is a comment on it.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

author.description: a guest's comment is a Note by a Person

about.description: one record makes it a comment; several make a CRM note

x-model.name: note
x-model.agent_context:
Note is the only place for commentary; a conversation with a customer is Messages. Always set about (the records
it concerns) and author. Dedupe by identifier only. The one mistake: visibility shared on a Note meant for the
team; shared Notes are readable by the end users who can read the record they are about.

Organization.title: Organization
Organization.description: A company, nonprofit, government body or household: a customer, a vendor, a partner or an account. The relationship to the workspace lives on Deals, Invoices, affiliations and tags, never on the Organization.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

addresses.description: kind billing, shipping, mailing, work or other

x-model.name: organization
x-model.agent_context:
Use Organization for any company or institution. Dedupe by the domain identifier (identifiers [{system: domain,
value: ...}]); derive the domain from a website URL before creating, and add vat:*, duns or lei identifiers when
known. Firmographics (industry, employees, annual revenue) are ext.crm.*, the registered name for invoices is
ext.billing.legal_name, and the relationship (customer, partner, vendor) is a tag. The one mistake: a second
Organization for the same company under another spelling of its name.

Person.title: Person
Person.description: A human being: a customer, a contact, an employee, or an end user of the product.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

phones.description: label mobile, home, fax, work or other

urls.description: websites and social profiles; the URL identifies the network

affiliations.description: Organizations this person belongs to, with role, primary flag and period

timezone.description: IANA zone; the OIDC zoneinfo claim

x-model.name: person
x-model.agent_context:
Use Person for any human, whatever their role. Roles live on relationships (affiliations, Deal.people,
Ticket.requester), never on the Person; a lead is a Person with ext.crm.lifecycle_stage lead. Dedupe by email:
before creating, query by emails.value or use upsert. An end user of the product is a Person that holds an
Identity; you never create Identities yourself. The one mistake: a second Person for the same human under another
email; add the address to emails[] instead.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: A thing the business sells or buys: a good, a service or a digital item. What it costs lives on a Price in the Billing pack.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

unit.description: default unit of measure for invoice lines: a UN/ECE Rec 20 code (C62, HUR) or a word (seat, hour)

tax_rate.description: the default tax rate for lines of this product

x-model.name: product
x-model.agent_context:
One Product per sellable thing, never one per price: the amount, currency and billing interval live on Prices
that reference it, and a plan billed monthly and yearly is one Product with two Prices. Dedupe by the sku
identifier (system sku). Inventory counts, purchase cost and ledger accounts are extensions. The one mistake:
deleting a Product that Invoices or Subscriptions reference; set active to false instead.

Project.title: Project
Project.description: A container of work with a lifecycle: planned, active, paused, done or cancelled. Tasks belong to it.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

archived_at.description: hidden from default views; independent of status

x-model.name: project
x-model.agent_context:
Project is the container Tasks belong to; link it to what it is for through about (the client Organization, the
Deal). Dedupe by identifier only, so check for an existing Project by name before creating one. archived_at
hides it from default views and is independent of status. The one mistake: marking a Project done while Tasks
in it are still open.

Task.title: Task
Task.description: A unit of work with a status, a priority, assignees and a due date. It nests under a parent Task and belongs to one Project.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

due_at.description: set only when the source has a time of day

x-model.name: task
x-model.agent_context:
Task is work someone has to do; a reminder at a time is an Event, a request from a customer is a Ticket. Use
due_on for a date and due_at only when the source has a time of day. Blocked is a state label under open or
in_progress, not a category. Dedupe by identifier only, so search open Tasks by title before creating one.
The one mistake: setting status.category to done without completed_at; set both.

Team.title: Team
Team.description: A named group of Members that work is assigned to.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

x-model.name: team
x-model.agent_context:
Team groups Members of this workspace (operators), not Persons; a customer's departments are Organizations with a
parent. Dedupe by a source identifier, then by name. Hierarchy, group type and a lead are ext.org.*; the
accountable operator is the envelope's owner. The one mistake: adding a Person to members; only Members belong.

Deal.title: Deal
Deal.description: A potential sale to an Organization or a Person, tracked through a Pipeline, with an amount, a probability and an expected close. Won or lost is the status category.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

stage.description: a stage key of the pipeline

status.description: category defaults from the stage's category

x-model.name: deal
x-model.agent_context:
Deal is the opportunity, not the customer: the customer is the Organization or Person it points at. Set stage
to a key of its Pipeline; status.category follows that stage's category unless you set it (a deal can be lost
from any stage), and won emits deal.won. people[] holds the contacts on the deal, one marked primary. Dedupe by
identifier only, so query open Deals for the same Organization before creating one. The one mistake: products,
quantities and prices on the Deal; they belong on the quote or the Invoice.

Pipeline.title: Pipeline
Pipeline.description: An ordered set of stages that Deals move through, each mapped to one of the standard categories open, won or lost. A workspace has one default pipeline.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

default.description: the pipeline new Deals go to when none is given

archived.description: retired; kept because Deals still reference it

x-model.name: pipeline
x-model.agent_context:
Read the default pipeline before creating a Deal and use one of its stage keys; Deal.pipeline is required and
the default pipeline is used when you omit it. Every pipeline holds at least one open, one won and one lost
stage. Dedupe by name. The one mistake: deleting or re-keying a stage that Deals reference; set archived true
and keep the key.

Invoice.title: Invoice
Invoice.description: A statement of money owed for goods or services: receivable when we issued it, payable when we received it (a bill). Lines with amounts and taxes, totals, a status from draft to paid, and the payments applied to it.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

number.description: required once status is not draft; unique per workspace when receivable, per counterparty when payable

direction.description: a bill is a payable Invoice

bill_to.description: the billing address as printed; defaults from the counterparty

due_at.description: due_at or terms is given when amount_due is above zero

terms.description: payment terms as text, e.g. Net 30

currency.description: ISO 4217; every Money on the invoice uses it

unit.description: unit of measure; a UN/ECE Rec 20 code or a word

discount.description: line-level discount already deducted from amount

amount.description: the line total as billed: normally quantity times unit_price minus discount, including tax only when tax_inclusive; prorated or rounded lines may differ, so it is not checked against them

period.description: the service period the line covers

memo.description: a customer-facing note printed on the invoice

x-model.name: invoice
x-model.agent_context:
Create with status draft; number may be empty until the invoice leaves draft, then it is required and unique per
workspace for receivable invoices and per counterparty for payable ones. subtotal is the sum of lines.amount,
total is subtotal minus discount_total plus tax_total (tax_total excluded when tax_inclusive), amount_due is
total minus amount_paid (zero on a void invoice); overdue and partially paid are queries, not statuses. The one mistake: status paid
without a Payment; create the Payment, apply it, then set paid and paid_at, which emits invoice.paid.

Payment.title: Payment
Payment.description: Money that moved against invoices: a customer paying us (receivable), us paying a vendor (payable), or a refund of either.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

reference.description: check number, bank reference, processor id or remittance text

x-model.name: payment
x-model.agent_context:
direction is the ledger side; kind says whether money went the normal way (payment) or back (refund, with
refund_of pointing at the original). applied[] says which Invoices this payment settles and by how much; update
their amount_paid and status yourself. Payments recorded from accounting systems are succeeded; processor payments
carry pending, failed or cancelled. Dedupe by identifier (the processor's or ledger's id). The one mistake: a
refund as a negative amount; record a Payment of kind refund.

Price.title: Price
Price.description: An amount at which a Product is sold, once or on a recurring interval. Subscription items and Invoice lines point at Prices.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

name.description: a short label: Monthly, Annual, 2 seats

amount.description: per unit, per interval; tax per tax_inclusive

interval_count.description: intervals between charges; 3 with month bills quarterly

x-model.name: price
x-model.agent_context:
interval one_time is a one-off price; any other interval with interval_count makes it recurring (month with
interval_count 3 bills quarterly). Metered usage, tiers and trials are ext.billing.*. Dedupe by an identifier
(the billing provider's price id) or by (product, name). The one mistake: changing the amount of a Price that
Subscriptions use; create a new Price and set active false on the old one.

Subscription.title: Subscription
Subscription.description: A recurring agreement to bill (receivable) or be billed (payable) for Prices, period after period. Each period's charge is an Invoice that points back at it.

source.description: {system, external_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at?, import_run, imported_at, payload}

direction.description: receivable = our customer; payable = a vendor we pay

current_period.description: the period being billed now; absent while pending

cancel_at.description: scheduled end; when set the subscription does not renew

reference.description: the customer's PO or reference, copied onto generated invoices

x-model.name: subscription
x-model.agent_context:
Subscription is the recurring relationship; each period's charge is an Invoice that references it. status pending
means it exists but has not started, so current_period and started_at are absent; cancel_at set means it will
not renew; ended_at is when it stopped. Dedupe by identifier (the billing provider's subscription id). The one
